answer: The forge multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and juniper lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2643 identities would post 2736 proofs and burn roughly 20 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
